title: 専門教養特別科目（麹・発酵食品の歴史と科学）
subtitle: Special Subject - Specialties Education(History and Science of Koji and Fermented Foods)
courseType: （Provided by all courses）Liberal Arts CoursesTransdisciplinary Learning
educationalGoal:
To understand the mechanism of “koji” from historical and scientific viewpoints.
To understand the mechanism of “koji mold” from the viewpoint of molecular biology and genetics.
To understand the mechanism of “fermented food” from a biochemical point of view.
To understand the origins of Ishikawa's fermentation industry from historical and cultural perspectives.
advice:
The purpose of this lecture is to learn more about “fermentation” from a scientific viewpoint by learning about “koji” and “koji mold,” which are indispensable to Ishikawa's fermentation industry.
The lecture will focus on “koji” and “koji mold,” both of which are essential to Ishikawa's fermentation industry.　Koji has long been used in traditional Japanese foods. Especially in Ishikawa, koji is used not only for sake, soy sauce, miso, and vinegar, but also for kabura-zushi, etc.
It is used not only for sake, soy sauce, miso, and vinegar, but also for kabura-zushi (turnip sushi), and is very familiar in Ishikawa compared to other regions. However, the fact that the koji fungus is a “national fungus” and that it is used in Takaoka and Kanazawa is not well known.
It is not well known, however, that the koji is a “national fungus” and that Dr. Jokichi Takamine, a great man from Takaoka and Kanazawa, used fusuma koji to produce “takadia starase”.
It is not well known. The goal of this course is to learn about koji mold, the “national fungus,” and “koji” made with koji mold, to follow in the footsteps of local greats, and to gain a deeper understanding of the fermentation industry in Japan and Ishikawa.
The aim is to gain a deep understanding of the fermentation industry in Japan and Ishikawa.
requiredKnowledge:
Knowledge of biology at the college level, basic (first or second year of college in biotechnology) biochemistry, molecular biology, and genetics is desirable.
The candidate should have a basic knowledge of biochemistry, molecular biology, and genetics at a college level.
